instruction: Our SFTP alarm {{reference-architectures-Transfer-sftp-us-east-1-AlarmName}} on server {{reference-architectures-Transfer-sftp-us-east-1-ServerId}} never fires even when we see errors in the logs. What does it actually take to trigger it, and will anyone be notified when it does?
expected_answer: The alarm {{reference-architectures-Transfer-sftp-us-east-1-AlarmName}} watches a custom metric SftpErrors (namespace SFTP/Transfer) that a metric filter on log group {{reference-architectures-Transfer-sftp-us-east-1-LogGroupName}} increments on the literal string "ERROR"; it triggers on Sum >= 1 with TreatMissingData=notBreaching. It never fires because that log group receives no data. The Transfer server uses a legacy loggingRole with no structuredLogDestinations, so AWS Transfer Family logs to the service-managed group /aws/transfer/<server-id>, not {{reference-architectures-Transfer-sftp-us-east-1-LogGroupName}}. With nothing published to SftpErrors, the alarm stays in INSUFFICIENT_DATA (treated as OK) and cannot reach ALARM from real errors. Even if it did fire, no one would be notified: AlarmActions is empty. Fix: route the server's logs to {{reference-architectures-Transfer-sftp-us-east-1-LogGroupName}} (add structuredLogDestinations, or repoint the metric filter to /aws/transfer/<server-id>) so ERROR events increment SftpErrors, and add an SNS topic ARN to AlarmActions.
